schema_notes: `required` is tri-state: true = the command cannot act without the key on any path; false = optional on every path; "conditional" = required only inside a branch, the branch named in the key's `notes` and in the command's `branches`.

`branches` (added field) -- several handlers are selector-shaped (`action`, `pen`, `hidden`, `loading`): a flat required/optional split would misstate them. Each row: selector, requires, optional, effect, source.
`value_docs` (added field) -- where a key is enumerated and each value selects a different effect, C6's per-thing doc line is attached per value, not only per key.
`key_grammar` (added field) -- for the two commands whose key is not from a fixed list: `flag` (key = a flag name, cross-ref families.flags) and `print` (key = anything the author writes).

`downstream` (added field, boolean) -- key not read in this line range: the handler forwards the whole args map and the key is read in another file. Anchored there. Such keys consume NO row of the count gate.

Absent-key value for every eval* conversion is fixed IN the handler file and is not opaque: evalDouble("")=0.0, evalInt("")=0, evalString("")="" [app_command_interface.cpp:4458-4479]. What a NON-empty string evaluates to stays opaque here (app_command_eval.cpp, INTENT S5 item 5): recorded as evalDouble/evalInt/evalString, $-variable substitution possible.

shared_context.executeCommandStatus: app_command_interface.cpp:1163-1177 -- the return path of every handler. debug_message EMPTY = success: the line is recorded when recording is on and 'true' is returned. debug_message SET = two log lines ('Could not execute: <line>' + the message) and 'false'. A handler that returns without setting debug_message therefore reports SUCCESS even when it did nothing.

flag.doc: Turn a named display feature on, off, or to the opposite of what it is now.

key_grammar.doc: One pair: the KEY is the name of the feature, the VALUE says on, off or toggle.
key_grammar.key_domain: families.flags -- the 97 registered flag names (app_command_init.cpp:133-229); an unregistered name gives 'Unrecognized or malformed flag argument'
values: any on-form accepted by Utility::isTrue (src/tools/utility.hpp:160-171: "1", "on"/"ON", "true"/"TRUE", case-insensitive)

notes: SINGLE PAIR ONLY, and it is the ALPHABETICALLY FIRST key of the line, not the first written: the handler reads args.begin() and never loops (the code says so itself: '// could loop if want to allow that syntax', :1345). 'flag stars on nebulae off' applies only 'nebulae off'. Confirms parse_model.flag_multi_pair.

Recording rewrite: when the value is exactly 'toggle', the line stored by the recorder becomes '<command> <key> <0|1>' with the state the toggle produced (:1352-1356) -- a recorded script replays a state, not a toggle. `val` is a bool streamed with operator<<, so the recorded spelling is '0'/'1' (both are legal values: utility.hpp:167,179).
Per-flag documentation is NOT part of this unit (SWEEP_DISPATCH DoD 6): only the key grammar shape is recorded here.

get.doc: Ask the running program for one piece of information and send the answer back over the network connection.

value_docs.planets_position: One entry per non-satellite body, 'name:x:y:z;', its position around the Sun multiplied by 100 and rounded (src/bodyModule/protosystem.cpp:451-465). If the text comes back empty the reply sent is the literal 'NPF' (app_command_interface.cpp:1376-1379).
value_docs.constellation: The short name of the constellation currently selected (src/coreModule/coreLink.cpp:553).
value_docs.object: The several-line description of the object currently selected (src/coreModule/core.hpp:386-389). If empty the reply sent is the literal 'EOL' (app_command_interface.cpp:1383-1386).
value_docs.media: How far the video has played, as 'mm:ss / mm:ss speed <factor>' (src/mediaModule/video_player.cpp:134-141). If empty the reply sent is 'NMF', which the code glosses as 'No media file' (app_command_interface.cpp:1388-1391).

notes: This is the one handler in the unit that forwards the WHOLE parsed map (:1681, :1683, :1686): its key vocabulary is not visible in this file at all, and any key the author invents is carried along and ignored silently.

C1-relevant: `args["color_tex"]` at :1680 and `args["maxobject"]` at :1685 are std::map::operator[] reads, which INSERT an empty entry for an absent key. The map handed downstream therefore differs from the map the line actually wrote -- for these two keys the downstream reads (`find` at dsoNavigator.cpp:264-265, `operator[]` at :321) treat empty and absent alike, so no behaviour changes today; a tool that models 'the keys of this line' must still know the insertion happens.

The four literal key spellings here ("color_tex", "alpha_tex", "depth", "maxobject" at :1680-1688) are written as bare strings, not W_* tokens -- only "maxobject" has a W_* twin (W_MAX_OBJECT, base_command_interface.hpp:100), and the handler does not use it.
